# Make Study Flashcards from Your Class Notes with DeepSeek: A Beginner's Guide

> **In short:** Paste a page of your notes into DeepSeek, ask for question-and-answer flashcards, then quiz yourself by covering the answers. Check every card against your notes, because the AI can make mistakes. Access and features may change, so confirm the current details on DeepSeek's official website.

You will learn how to turn any page of class notes or a textbook section into a set of flashcards, then test yourself with them. This guide is for students of any age and anyone studying for a class, exam, or certification. You don't need any experience with AI, only your notes and about 20 minutes.

## Before you start

- **A DeepSeek account or access.** Go to DeepSeek's official website or download its official app. You may be able to start without signing up, but signing up with an email address usually keeps your chats saved.
- **Your notes, typed or copied.** Have one page or one section ready. Typed text works best. Handwriting in a photo may not be read accurately.
- **About 20 to 30 minutes** for the whole process, including checking your cards.

## Step 1 — Open DeepSeek and start a new chat

Open DeepSeek in your web browser or the app on your phone. You should see an empty chat screen with a message box near the bottom, where you type. If you were already in an older conversation, look for a button like "New chat" or a plus sign, usually near the top or in a side panel, to start fresh. Starting fresh keeps your flashcards separate from other topics.

DeepSeek works by reading what you type and writing a reply, a bit like a tutor who reads your message and answers it. It doesn't know your class unless you tell it, so the next step gives it your material.

If the layout looks different on your device, don't worry. The message box is the one thing you need, and it is almost always at the bottom of the screen.

You'll know it worked when you can see an empty chat with the message box ready for typing.

## Step 2 — Paste your notes with a clear instruction

Copy one page of your notes or textbook section, then click or tap inside the message box and paste it. Press Enter or tap the send button, which is usually an arrow or paper-plane icon beside the box. Put your instruction before or after the notes so DeepSeek knows the job. Keep your request short and specific.

It's best to paste no more than a page or two at a time. Very long text can be harder to process well, and shorter sections give you more accurate cards.

💬 Example: "Here are my notes on [your subject]. Make 15 flashcards from them. Write each one as a Question line followed by an Answer line, and use only facts from my notes."

You'll know it worked when DeepSeek replies with a list of question and answer pairs. Typing begins as soon as the reply starts, so give it a few seconds to finish.

## Step 3 — Check every card against your notes

Read each card and compare it with the original notes. Look for wrong dates, names, or definitions, and for questions that don't match the notes. AI can sound confident and still get a detail wrong, so treat the cards as a first draft. If a card is wrong, ask DeepSeek to fix it by typing a correction, which keeps the rest of the chat in context.

This checking step is also a great study session. Reading the notes again while you check helps the material stick.

💬 Example: "Card 4 is wrong. My notes say the answer is [correct answer], so please rewrite that card."

If you can't find a fact in your notes, cross it out or delete it from your final set. Never study from a card you can't verify.

You'll know it worked when every card matches your notes and you feel comfortable with each answer.

## Step 4 — Save the cards in a format you can use

Once your cards look right, ask DeepSeek to reformat them into a table. A two-column table with "Question" on one side and "Answer" on the other is easy to copy into a document, a notes app, or a printed sheet. You can also copy the text straight from the chat and paste it into a notes app on your phone so you have it anywhere.

Some people like to write the cards by hand, which can help memory even more. Either way, saving the cards outside the chat means you won't lose them if you start a new conversation later.

💬 Example: "Put all the flashcards into a two-column table, with Question on the left and Answer on the right."

If the table looks cramped or the text breaks oddly, copy the plain text instead and paste it into a document. Formatting can vary between devices, so your saved copy doesn't need to look perfect.

You'll know it worked when you have a clean list of cards saved in a place you can open again.

## Step 5 — Quiz yourself by covering the answers

Now the real study begins. Fold a piece of paper over the answer column, or use your hand to cover it. Read a question, say your answer out loud or write it down, then uncover the answer and compare. Mark the cards you got wrong, and put them in a separate pile to review more often.

You can also let DeepSeek act as your quiz partner. Ask it to show one question at a time and wait for your reply before continuing. This works well because you have to answer before you see the solution.

💬 Example: "Quiz me on these flashcards one at a time. Ask one question, wait for my answer, then tell me if I'm right before asking the next one."

DeepSeek can't check your facts against your textbook on its own, and it can't tell how well you remember the material. Your own honest answers and your missed-card pile are what truly show what to study next.

You'll know it worked when you finish a round and can name the specific cards you missed.

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting every card without checking.** AI can mix up facts. Fix it by comparing each card with your notes before you study, and deleting any card you can't verify.
- **Pasting too much at once.** A whole chapter can produce vague or messy cards. Fix it by working in sections of a page or two, then combining the finished sets.
- **Only reading the answers.** Reading the cards feels productive, but it doesn't test memory. Fix it by covering the answers, answering out loud, and only then checking.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use this for a recipe list, a language vocabulary sheet, or a driving-test handbook. Paste the text and quiz yourself on it.
- **For your business or work:** Turn a training manual or a set of product notes into quick reference cards for a new team member, and check the answers against the official document.
- **If you're just getting started:** Pick one short set of notes, such as a single lecture page, and go through Steps 2 to 5 once. The whole thing takes less than half an hour.

## Try it now

Open DeepSeek, paste five or six lines from tonight's reading, and type: "Make 5 question-and-answer flashcards from this text, using only facts from the text." Then cover the answers and quiz yourself on all five.
